Subject: Backup purge schedule + immutable snapshots question

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you had a good weekend. We're finalizing the DPA review for VoltHealth and noticed the backup purge timelines and log retention sections. Two asks from our side:

1) For regulated incident response we need a 30-day rollback/restore window for a read-only immutable snapshot (immutable snapshot = point-in-time locked copy) that can't be deleted by automated purge during that range. Can Redwood support an "escape hatch" that pins a snapshot for up to 30 days when triggered by a customer legal hold or security incident?

2) We also need visibility into the retention/era­se workflow for ephemeral logs (request/id mappings) — specifically: where are the logs stored, who is the subprocessor (if any), and how quickly can Redwood produce a tamper-evident exported archive for auditors?

We want suggested contract language (DPA clause) and any implementation notes you can share so our legal team can sign off.

Thanks,
Dri

VoltHealth

Dri / Vanessa / Marcus —

Thanks — we've drafted suggested DPA text and an operational runbook. High level:

- Contract language (suggested): "Customer-initiated Immutable Snapshot: Redwood Inference will, upon Customer's written request (including executive-level sign-off for legal holds), create a read-only immutable snapshot of Customer data and associated runtime logs. Redwood will mark the snapshot as protected from automated purge for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days (the 'Rollback Window'). Redwood will provide the Customer with a checksum and tamper-evident bundle for forensic analysis. The creation and release of such snapshot are subject to Redwood's documented operational procedure and audit trail."

- Operational flow: request submitted via Support Portal or a signed email to security@redwood.ai; Ops validates identity (SAML + contractual contact) within 4 business hours; snapshot creation and stabilization within 24 hours; export/tamper-evident bundle delivered within 48 hours of snapshot stabilization.

- Subprocessor notes: logs used for the export are stored in our encrypted object store (S3-compatible) in the US region. We use CloudVault (ops-support@cloudvault.io) as an object-storage subprocessor for long-term archival. Exports include a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums) and an access log. We will add CloudVault as a named subprocessor in the DPA exhibit; any customer wanting alternate handling (on-prem escrow or different subprocessor) will require a commercial addendum.

- Exceptions and limits: snapshots are point-in-time copies and may not preserve in-flight ephemeral data; retention during the rollback window only prevents automated purges — manual deletion still requires documented joint authorization. Snapshots count against customer's storage quota; excessive use may be limited by capacity controls in Dedicated contracts.

I've attached a draft policy that Marcus and I iterated on. Marcus: please confirm the 24h/48h ops SLAs and any technical caveats (KV cache vs persisted logs).

Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quick technical confirmation and a couple of caveats:

- We can create an immutable snapshot and pin it for up to 30 days. For hosted customers the snapshot is implemented as an immutable object plus a metadata flag in our orchestration layer that excludes it from automated lifecycle rules. For Dedicated customers we can provide a second copy in a locked bucket.

- SLA timings Kimberly proposed are achievable but optimistic for cross-region restores during peak; suggest language: snapshot creation within 24 hours (typical 6-12 hours), export bundle ready within 72 hours in worst-case. If the request is tied to legal e-discovery we recommend using the signed-email + SSO verification flow Kimberly described to avoid delays.

- Logs: runtime request logs (request IDs, headers, routing) live in a short-lived hot store for 7 days by default, and then go to our cold archive (CloudVault) for 90 days before normal purge. The export will pull both current hot logs and archived files; CloudVault is a subprocessor for archive retrievals.

- Tamper-evident bundle: we generate a gzipped tar with a manifest and PGP-signed checksum file. We can include a chain-of-custody log as an addendum.

Dri — happy to run through the runbook via quick call if you want to validate the timings. If VoltHealth needs the 48-hour export SLA as firm, we should move to a Dedicated + addendum pricing conversation.

Marcus Lin
Director, Inference Operations, Redwood Inference
